content: 1. The International Health Regulations (IHR) core capacities are assessed over time using a structured Excel Spreadsheet File Model, which is divided into eight distinct modules. Each module serves a specific purpose in evaluating and documenting the core capacities of Points of Entry (PoE) as per IHR Annex 1B. 2. The first module, Summary, provides a comprehensive evaluation of the PoE's core capacities, highlighting strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement. It includes comments and suggestions for future enhancements. 3. The second module, All Groups of Core Capacities, summarizes the evaluation results for each core capacity group. 4. The third module, PoE ID, contains information about the identification of Points of Entry, enabling assessors to input and manage data efficiently. 5. The fourth module, Coordination and Communication, collects information on the core capacity requirements for coordination, event communication, and the implementation of measures. 6. The fifth module, Core Capacity at All Times (Routine), addresses questions related to the routine core capacity requirements for designated airports, ports, and ground crossings. 7. The sixth module, Core Capacity for Responding to Public Health Emergencies of International Concern (PHEIC), gathers information on the core capacity requirements for responding to events that may constitute PHEICs. 8. The seventh module, Reference, provides WHO-published guidelines relevant to the technical issues addressed by the assessment tool. 9. The eighth module, Language, ensures the spreadsheet can be used in English or other languages, with English as the default. It is critical not to modify the technical content of the worksheet, as all modules are interlinked, and changes may disrupt the entire spreadsheet. 10. The assessment process is recommended to be conducted by public health specialists with expertise in IHR core capacity requirements and PoE operations. The process involves sufficient input to ensure an objective evaluation. 11. At least two experts should collaborate on the assessment. In addition to using the electronic and paper versions of the Core Capacity Assessment Tool, assessors should document their observations with a notebook and a digital camera. 12. The assessment should be conducted during working hours to observe field operations at the PoE. It begins with a meeting to introduce the assessment team, outline objectives, and confirm stakeholder willingness to participate. 13. Assessors should review all relevant guidelines, management documents, standard operating procedures (SOPs), memoranda of understanding (MoUs), and protocols mentioned in the assessment tool. 14. During the field test, assessors should walk through areas related to public health operations, complete the checklist, and document observations with clear comments. Photographs of the PoE, staff, facilities, equipment, and operations should be taken to illustrate the core capacity conditions for the final report. 15. The Core Capacity Assessment Tool can initially be completed on paper for convenience. Once the visual evaluation is complete, the data should be transferred to the Excel Spreadsheet File Model. 16. To complete the modules, assessors should first select the appropriate language in the Language module. Then, they should proceed to the PoE ID sheet and select answers from the dropdown menu (Yes, No, or Partial). All grey cells in the Coordination and Communication, Core Capacity at All Times, and Core Capacity at PHEIC sheets must be filled in. 17. The results are automatically calculated in the All Groups sheet, and assessors should input comments and suggestions in the text boxes provided. They may also insert photographs or video clips as evidence. 18. Each question in the tool has limited possible answers: Yes (fully implemented), No (not implemented), or Partial (partially implemented). If the answer lies between two options, the most accurate one should be chosen systematically. 19. For example, if the answer is Yes in a few cases but Partial in most cases, the assessor should select Partial. This systematic approach ensures consistency and comparability across assessments. 20. Assessors must complete the assessment by inputting comments and suggestions in the summary worksheet, highlighting areas needing regulatory clarification or improvement to achieve full implementation of IHR core capacities. 21. Results are calculated based on the following principles: Yes answers receive 1 point (100%), No answers receive 0 points (0%), and Partial answers receive 0.5 points (50%). The final result is the average of all questions and is displayed at the top of the relevant column. 22. The results are expressed with background colors: red (below 50%) indicates significant improvement is needed, yellow (50%-80%) indicates some improvement is needed, and green (above 80%) indicates the PoE is fairly consistent with IHR Annex 1 requirements. 23. The final results are reflected numerically and graphically in the Summary worksheet, with space provided for assessors to input comments and captured evidence (e.g., photographs, video clips, and observations). 24. Each worksheet in the Excel Spreadsheet File Model can be protected against modifications to prevent errors that may compromise calculations. To protect a worksheet, click Tools, then Protection, and Protect Sheet, and input the pre-set password. 25. To unprotect a worksheet, click Tools, then Protection, and Unprotect Sheet. It is recommended to save the work under a different name before unprotecting to preserve the original file. 26. The evaluation of results should be conducted after all data and comments on strengths, weaknesses, and plans for future improvements have been input. The results will be expressed with different background colors and reflected in both numerical and graphical forms in the Summary worksheet.
